description.en: The constituent states of four federations and their capitals, as of October 2026: Germany's 16 and Austria's 9 states, Canada's 10 provinces and 3 territories, and Australia's 6 states and 2 self-governing mainland territories, 46 cards. Front: the state, province or territory, e.g. "Bavaria" (Swedish "Bayern"), with its country in a note; back: its capital, e.g. "Munich" ("München"). For Berlin, Hamburg and Vienna, cities that are themselves states, the answer is the city itself. Taken from Wikidata and checked against official sites of each country, the Swedish Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin.
description.sv: Delstaterna i fyra förbundsstater och deras huvudstäder, enligt läget i oktober 2026: Tysklands 16 och Österrikes 9 förbundsländer, Kanadas 10 provinser och 3 territorier samt Australiens 6 delstater och 2 självstyrande fastlandsterritorier, 46 kort. Framsida: delstaten, provinsen eller territoriet, t.ex. ”Bayern”, med landet i en anteckning; baksida: huvudstaden, t.ex. ”München”. För Berlin, Hamburg och Wien, städer som själva är förbundsländer, är svaret staden själv. Uppgifterna är hämtade från Wikidata och kontrollerade mot officiella webbplatser i varje land, svenskspråkiga Wikipedia och Nationalencyklopedin.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

1. Selection and capitals from Wikidata (query 1): every P150 (contains the administrative territorial entity) statement without an end time of Germany (Q183), Austria (Q40), Canada (Q16) and Australia (Q408), with the classes (P31) of each division, its P36 (capital) statements without an end time and their rank, and the English, Swedish and multilingual (mul) labels of division and capital. It returned 16 German divisions, all instances of "federated state of Germany" (Q1221156); 9 Austrian ones, all instances of "federal state of Austria" (Q261543); 13 Canadian ones, 10 instances of "province of Canada" (Q11828004) and 3 of "territory of Canada" (Q9357527); and 15 Australian ones: 6 instances of "state of Australia" (Q5852411), 3 "mainland territories of Australia" (Q14192234: the Australian Capital Territory, the Northern Territory and the Jervis Bay Territory) and 7 external territories. Every division in the deck has exactly one P36 statement without an end time, except Berlin (Q64), Hamburg (Q1055) and Vienna (Q1741), which have none: each is a single item that is both a city and a state (P31 includes Q133442, city-state). Query 2 read the further statements used in notes (Bremen's P150 and the P1448 official names of Klagenfurt and Quebec City) and the class and location of Q21882134, to confirm that this P36 value of Vorarlberg is the town of Bregenz.

2. Names from Wikidata (the script entities.py, query 3): the Wikidata API (wbgetentities) returned the English, Swedish, multilingual and German labels and aliases, the English and Swedish Wikipedia sitelinks and the claims of every division and capital of query 1 and of the class items. The front is the division's English and Swedish label. The back is the capital's English and Swedish label, with two exceptions: Fredericton (Q2138) has no English label, so its multilingual label is used; the English back of Carinthia is "Klagenfurt", the city's multilingual alias and the form the Austrian government table, NE and the Swedish label use, rather than the English label "Klagenfurt am Wörthersee", its official name (P1448), which the card gives in a note. The front notes give the federation and the kind of division in the compiler's own short wording, based on the class items Q1221156, Q261543, Q11828004, Q9357527, Q5852411 and Q14192234 (sv labels "förbundsland", "Österrikes förbundsländer", "provins i Kanada", "territorium i Kanada", "delstat i Australien", "fastlandsterritorium i Australien"): "Förbundsland i Tyskland", "Förbundsland i Österrike", "Provins i Kanada", "Territorium i Kanada", "Delstat i Australien", "Territorium i Australien".

3. Official checks, one per federation, each page downloaded with curl (queries 4 to 7) and its text read after removing the HTML tags: Germany — the Bundesrat's page "Die Länder", whose box for each Land gives "Hauptstadt: …" for all 16 ("Berlin Hauptstadt: Berlin", "Freie Hansestadt Bremen Hauptstadt: Bremen", "Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg Hauptstadt: Hamburg"); Austria — the federal government's Migration.gv.at page "Geografie und Bevölkerung", whose table ("Quelle: Statistik Austria (Stand 1.1.2026, vorläufige Daten)") gives the Landeshauptstadt of eight Länder and a dash for Wien; for Vienna the federal constitution (B-VG Art. 108, from the Austrian legal information system RIS, query 8) was read; Canada — the citizenship guide Discover Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada), chapter "Canada's Regions", whose table lists, per region, the provinces and territories and their capital cities in the same order; Australia — Tourism Australia's page "Australian States, Territories and Capital Cities", which names the capital in its section on each state and territory. The Australian government sources tried first gave no list of state capitals: Geoscience Australia's page on the areas of the states and territories and the Australian Bureau of Statistics' page on Greater Capital City Statistical Areas (both fetched, query 7) describe the capital cities without naming each state's capital, so they were not used. Each card's evidence quotes the line or sentence of the official page; the script make_dossier.py asserted that every quote occurs in the saved page text (with tags removed, white space collapsed and a space before a comma or full stop removed).

4. Swedish names (queries 9 and 10): the four Swedish Wikipedia list articles "Tysklands förbundsländer", "Österrikes förbundsländer", "Kanadas provinser och territorier" and "Australiens delstater och territorier" were fetched as wikitext with their revision ids through the MediaWiki API (svwiki.py) and the division and capital cells of their tables parsed (parse_svwiki.py). For every card the Swedish front equals the name shown in the row and the Swedish back equals the capital's link text (for the city-states, the German table spans the row of Berlin and Hamburg over both columns, with the note "Berlin och Hamburg är både städer och förbundsländer", and the Austrian table has a dash for Wien). Nationalencyklopedin was then consulted (fetch_ne.py): the article on each division whose address could be found from its Swedish or English name (34 of the 46; Berlin, Hamburg, Bremen, Brandenburg, Saarland, Schleswig-Holstein, Salzburg, Alberta, Manitoba, Ontario, Saskatchewan and Victoria were not fetched or not found, and those cards rest on Wikidata, the official page and the Swedish Wikipedia), and the articles on München, Hannover, Düsseldorf, Sankt Pölten, Klagenfurt, Eisenstadt, Bregenz, Quebec (the city) and Canberra. The evidence quotes NE's short description phrase (e.g. "delstat i södra Tyskland") and, where present, the phrase naming the capital. Where NE's Swedish form differs from the card (Quebec, Newfoundland and Labrador, compounds written with an en dash) the card follows Wikidata's Swedish label and the Swedish Wikipedia; see quality control.

5. Assembly: make_dossier.py wrote the cards from the saved files: the Wikidata evidence from q1.csv and entities.json, the Swedish Wikipedia evidence from the parsed rows, and the official and NE evidence from the quotes listed in the script, each asserted to be present in the saved page. It also refuses a card whose division is not in query 1, is not an instance of its class, whose capital is not its P36 value, or whose English or Swedish text is not a label, alias or mul label of the item. The Wikidata checks on every card (division labels, class, capital, capital labels, and the statements behind the notes) are run against live Wikidata by the builder on every build.

6. The city-state convention: where one item is both the city and the state (Berlin, Hamburg, Vienna), the card's answer is the city itself, with the note "City-state: the city is itself a state"; the Bundesrat states the same for Berlin and Hamburg ("Hauptstadt: Berlin", "Hauptstadt: Hamburg"). Bremen is a city-state of two cities whose capital is the city of Bremen (Wikidata P36, the Bundesrat). For Vienna no source names a separate capital (the Austrian table leaves it blank); the card applies the same convention, and its note states the fact the answer rests on, that the city is itself the state.
selection: All constituent states of four federations, as of 4 October 2026: the 16 Länder of Germany, the 9 Länder of Austria, the 10 provinces and 3 territories of Canada, and the 6 states and the 2 self-governing mainland territories of Australia (the Australian Capital Territory and the Northern Territory): 46 cards, one per division, each with its one current capital. Left out: Australia's Jervis Bay Territory (a mainland territory without self-government or a capital of its own; the Swedish Wikipedia and Wikidata list it separately) and its seven external territories (Norfolk Island, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and others), which are not among the states and self-governing territories of the federation; the federal capitals as such (Berlin, Vienna, Ottawa, Canberra), except where they are themselves a state's capital or a city-state, as noted on those cards; former capitals; and other federations (the United States has its own deck). Conventions: Berlin, Hamburg and Vienna, each a single city that is itself a state, are answered with the city itself (see the method); Canberra is the capital of the Australian Capital Territory as Wikidata and the Swedish Wikipedia list give it. The cards are studied front to back only: "Victoria" is both an Australian state (front) and the capital of British Columbia (back), and the city-states have the same name on both sides, so the reverse direction would not always have one answer.

licensing: The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of the 46 divisions, the link from each to its capital, the English and Swedish names, the class names in the front notes and the facts in the back notes all come from it, so the deck is CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The Bundesrat, Migration.gv.at, Discover Canada and Tourism Australia (all with copyright terms that allow at most non-commercial reproduction), Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only, as was the Austrian federal constitution on RIS (not protected by copyright, § 7 UrhG): they confirmed facts that Wikidata gave, and no wording, table or selection was copied from them. The selection is the complete set of constituent states of each federation, shared by any list of them because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from a list. The notes are the compiler's own wording. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the deck: they are short verbatim quotations naming their sources (for NE under the Swedish quotation right, Upphovsrättslagen 22 §, and in line with NE's own conditions for quoting).

rounds.lens: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's division, capital and names against Wikidata, the official page of its federation (Bundesrat, Migration.gv.at, Discover Canada, Tourism Australia), the Swedish Wikipedia list and, where found, Nationalencyklopedin; the city-state convention; the Swedish names.
rounds.scope: All 46 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.
rounds.summary: Wikidata, the official pages and the Swedish Wikipedia agree on the capital of every division that has one; NE agrees wherever an article was found. No Wikidata check was skipped. The differences found are the city-states (no separate capital in Wikidata, the Austrian table and the Swedish Wikipedia; the Bundesrat names Berlin and Hamburg as their own capitals), a few name forms (Klagenfurt, Quebec City, Yukon, Swedish forms in NE) and the name Victoria on both sides of the deck.

findings.issue: No source names a separate capital of the state of Vienna: Wikidata has no P36 on Q1741 (one item for the city and the state), the Austrian government table has a dash in the Landeshauptstadt column for Wien, and the Swedish Wikipedia table has "–". The B-VG speaks of "die Bundeshauptstadt Wien als Land" and NE calls Wien "huvudstad i Österrike och en av landets delstater".
findings.resolution: Kept with the city-state convention used for Berlin and Hamburg: the answer is the city itself, and the note says why ("City-state: the city is itself a state"). The convention is stated in the description, the method and the selection, and the Austrian table's dash is recorded in the card's evidence.

findings.issue: Berlin and Hamburg have no P36 in Wikidata (each is one item, both city and Land, P31 Q133442 city-state) and the Swedish Wikipedia table spans their row over the capital column; the Bundesrat gives "Berlin Hauptstadt: Berlin" and "Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg Hauptstadt: Hamburg".
